hero.title: Run many coding agents at once, and see what each one needs.
hero.lede: trace is a desktop app for Claude Code and Codex. Start agents on tickets, quick ideas or a schedule, each in its own git worktree or a Vercel Sandbox. Read each one as a chat, answer them all from one inbox, and see the whole fleet at a glance.
hero.alt: trace showing an agent's chat on the left, the files it changed with their diff on the right, and a terminal below running the tests: three passing.

features.label: Agents as a chat
features.title: Claude and Codex, as a conversation you can read
features.text: Agents run as a formatted chat rather than a wall of terminal output: Markdown replies, a card per tool call, the diff of every edit, and permission prompts answered where they appear. When an agent fans work out, each subagent gets a live card and its own tab.
points: Subagents as live cards, opened in a tab or beside the chat
Insight asides as callout cards; long tool output folds, with Show all
Copy any message from its hover bar, or a table for docs and spreadsheets
features.alt: A prompt asks the agent to add a delete() helper and a test. Tool cards appear as it reads the files, an edit waits for permission and Allow once is clicked, then the diff, the test run and a Markdown reply with a table of the tests; pointing at the reply shows its Copy button.

more.label: Subagents
more.alt: The agent starts two subagents in parallel. Two cards show them running; one is opened beside the chat, where its brief, a Read call and then its finished report appear while the other card turns to Done.

features.label: The composer
features.title: Pick the model, effort and mode as you write
features.text: A chat agent's composer keeps its model, effort and permission mode, switched live where the CLI allows. Type / for slash commands and your saved prompts, attach files and pictures, and leave a message half-written: it's still there after a restart. A ring in the chat header shows how full the context is.
points: Mode: Ask, Accept edits, Plan or Full access, kept for each agent
Saved prompts sent as /name, from Settings → Agents
Paste, drop or pick files; pictures show as thumbnails
features.alt: In a chat session the Model picker is opened and Opus chosen, then Effort set to High and Mode to Plan. Typing /rep lists a saved prompt, Enter puts its text in the box, a screenshot is pasted and shows as a thumbnail, and the message is sent; the context ring sits in the chat header.

features.label: Fleet
features.title: Every running agent at a glance
features.text: Fleet is a table of every live agent: its state, how long it's been there, its repo and branch, changes, PR and latest line. Rows stay put when an agent changes state, so you never lose your place, and an agent on a long task can leave a one-line progress note there.
points: Filter by Needs you, Working or Ready
Opened order, or drag to reorder
The latest thing each agent said, or the note it left
features.alt: The Fleet table with five agents: some Ready, two needing you and one Working. Filters for Needs you and Working are tried, and the working agent finishes while its row stays in place.

features.label: Inbox
features.title: One inbox for every question and approval
features.text: When any agent needs you, from the board, a session or a scheduled prompt, it lands in the Inbox with its question or the exact change it wants to make. Answer it there and the agent carries on; you don't have to find its tab first.
points: Questions with options, or your own answer
Approvals with the full command or edit
J and K to move, 1–9 to answer, E to dismiss
features.alt: The Inbox lists agents that need you. A question about default units is answered with Metric, then an agent's edit adding a --json flag is approved, and the next request arrives.

features.label: Panes, Files and Terminal
features.title: Chat, Files and Terminal, arranged like an IDE
features.text: Every agent's tabs can sit side by side or stacked: the conversation, the files it changed, and a shell in the same worktree. A tab shows up when there's something in it and hides with its ×; layouts are remembered per workspace. Quick Open finds any file in the worktree, and the terminal finds in its scrollback and has a menu on every file path.
points: Split right, split down, or drag a tab to any edge
Quick Open: ⌘P on macOS, Ctrl+Shift+P on Windows and Linux
Copy Context: the last 100 lines, headed with the agent and worktree
features.alt: From a single chat pane, Files is split to the right and Terminal moved below it. A shell opens in the agent's worktree, npm test runs and passes, and the changed test file's diff is shown.

more.label: Files and Quick Open
more.alt: In an agent's Files tab, All files shows the worktree's tree and a file is opened. Quick Open is then brought up, a few letters narrow it to router.test.ts, and Enter opens that file with its diff.

more.label: Terminal extras
more.alt: In an agent's shell, git status lists the two changed files. Right-clicking a file path opens a menu with Open in VS Code, IntelliJ or Cursor, Show in folder, Copy path, Copy context and Find; Find then highlights each match for router in the scrollback.

features.label: Plans, Browser and Gallery
features.title: What the agent planned and made, beside the chat
features.text: When an agent leaves plan mode or publishes a plan, spec or report, it opens in the Plan tab: Markdown set like a page, or HTML in a sandbox, with every version kept. An agent can also open its dev server in the Browser tab, an isolated view that gets nothing of trace's, or show you a folder of images in the Gallery.
points: Versions of each document, with the changes between any two
Copy, save as Markdown, HTML or PDF, or send to an agent as context
Gallery thumbnails fill in as files appear, with zoom and compare
features.alt: An agent is asked to publish a plan for adding middleware to a router. When its turn ends a Plan tab appears with a dot; it's opened, the document is scrolled from its goal to its tests, and the list of plans slides out from the left edge.

more.label: Gallery
more.alt: An agent is asked to draw four icons for a CLI's sort modes and show them. When its turn ends a Gallery tab appears; it's opened to a grid of the four icons, the first opens full size, and the arrow keys step through the rest.

more.label: Browser
more.alt: An agent's chat on the left and its Browser tab on the right, showing a local playground page for the tinyroute demo: its routes, with the new DELETE route marked, and a sample request.
more.caption: The Browser tab: a local page beside the agent, in its own isolated view.

features.label: Tickets and pull requests
features.title: From a Jira or Pylon ticket to a pull request
features.text: Connect Jira, Pylon or both, and each adds its board to the sidebar exactly as your tracker shows it. Start an agent on a card and it gets a new worktree and a kickoff prompt built from the ticket and its comments. When it raises a PR, the Pull request tab follows its checks and conversation, and Merge is in the header.
points: Your board's own columns, filters and sprints
Moving a card moves the ticket; auto-start is a setting
Checks and review threads, with what's new since you looked
features.alt: On a Jira board, a card is dragged to In Progress and its agent starts in a new worktree with the ticket as its brief. The agent's Pull request tab then shows its checks passing and a review comment, and the Merge button waits in the header.

placeholder.alt: trace's Integrations page: Jira, Pylon, GitHub and Vercel ready to connect, and Tailscale.
placeholder.caption: Shown without a tracker connected: no ticket data is made up for this page.

features.label: Run it anywhere
features.title: Sessions in a worktree, a folder or a Vercel Sandbox
features.text: Sessions are agents that aren't tied to a ticket. Each runs in its own git worktree of a repo you've added, in a folder you pick, or in a new empty folder that goes with it. Connect Vercel and a session can run in a Vercel Sandbox instead: Leave running keeps it working after you quit, and Start joins it again.
points: Started by you, another agent, the orchestrator or a schedule
Sort by status, name, age or who started them, or keep your own order
Stop & save snapshots a sandbox; Join picks one up from another computer
features.alt: The Sessions list is sorted by who started each session, which nests a session another agent started under that agent's session, then by status, then back to manual order. The agent-started session is opened, showing its repo, worktree branch and who started it.

features.label: Orchestrator
features.title: Ask what your agents are doing
features.text: The orchestrator sits in the side panel and knows your board and sessions. Ask it for a status round-up, what's blocked, or to nudge an agent; every action it takes waits for your confirm. Stats chart your agents and their work.
points: Your API key, or your logged-in Claude CLI
Charts of agents by state, and session stats
Actions behind a confirm card
features.alt: The orchestrator is asked what the agents are doing. It replies with a round-up: which agents are ready, which stopped and when, and the totals, then its Stats tab is opened.

features.label: Scheduled prompts
features.title: Prompts that run themselves, when there's something to do
features.text: Run a prompt every few minutes, daily, weekly, monthly or on a cron expression, each run a fresh conversation in the prompt's own worktree. A precheck command decides whether a run goes ahead, so a nightly job can skip the nights nothing changed. Continue as session picks up where any run left off.
points: Variables like {lastRunAt}, {date} and {repo}
Run history with each run's conversation
Import and export prompts to share them
features.alt: A new scheduled prompt called Morning test run is filled in: a prompt, a daily schedule, allowed tools and a precheck command that only runs it when the branch is behind. It's saved and its detail shows the precheck.

features.label: Coming from Conductor
features.title: Coming from Conductor? Bring your work with you
features.text: Settings → Repositories → Import from Conductor reads Conductor's database without changing it and shows what it found, with a checkbox each. Repos come over with their setup scripts, live workspaces move in as sessions that carry on the same conversation, and custom prompts become saved prompts.
points: Each workspace marked Resumable, Transcript missing or Folder missing
Conductor's API token and saved environment are never read
New to trace? The first run checks git, claude and gh, with fixes
features.alt: In Settings → Repositories, Import from Conductor is opened and Conductor is closed is clicked. The preview lists two repos with their setup translated, a live workspace marked Resumable and two custom prompts as saved prompts; the import runs, and its summary lists what came over and what was skipped.

features.label: Make it yours
features.title: Themes, fonts, density, sidebar and shortcuts
features.text: Dark, Light, Midnight, Paper or System, an accent colour, interface size and density, fonts for the UI, terminal and chat, each with a live preview. Density changes the whole app, and Compact tightens the chat's layout too. Order and hide the sidebar's pages, rebind every shortcut, and press ? for the cheat sheet.
points: Live previews, terminal schemes and cursor styles
One icon per action, named with its shortcut on hover
Every shortcut rebindable, shown in menus and the cheat sheet
features.alt: Settings → Appearance: the theme switches from Dark to Light, Paper and Midnight and back, with the previews updating; the accent and density change; then the Sidebar settings and the keyboard shortcut cheat sheet open.
